newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor wants prisoners to pay rent - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor wants prisoners to pay rent - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld is set to unveil a proposal on Wednesday that would require judges to order inmates at the time of sentencing to pay between five and 100 percent of the annual costs of their keep, The Boston Herald reported.

Massachusetts spends $300 million annually to house, feed and clothe 11,000 prisoners. The cost of housing an inmate at a maximum security facility costs more than $39,000 annually, while it runs about $30,000 at the house of corrections, the newspaper said.

"We decided a convicted felon should be responsible for all of the costs of their incarceration," an unnamed Weld administration source told the Herald. "We're going to squeeze as much out of this as we can."

The governor expects the program to generate about $3 million annually. He also intends to introduce legislation later Wednesday imposing a $5 co-payment on a prisoner each time he goes to the infirmary.
